name: Gerd Faltings
milestone_by_age_26: PhD at age 24 (1978) and habilitation thesis at 26 (1980) are standard academic qualifications; his landmark proof of the Mordell conjecture came at age 29 (1983) and the Fields Medal at 32 (1986). No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Faltings studied mathematics and physics at the University of Münster from 1972 to 1978, interrupted by military service, receiving his doctorate in 1978 at age 24. He completed his habilitation in 1981 at age 27.
evidence_summary: Faltings obtained his PhD at 24 and habilitation at 27, but his defining achievement—the proof of the Mordell conjecture—came at 29, earning him the Fields Medal at 32. No material milestone by age 26 was found beyond standard academic degrees.

name: Miquel Barceló
milestone_by_age_26: Participated as the only Spanish artist in Documenta 7 in Kassel, Germany, in 1982 at age 25, gaining international recognition.
early_history_summary: Born in Felanitx, Mallorca, Barceló studied at the Arts and Crafts School of Palma for two years before briefly enrolling at the Fine Arts School of Barcelona in 1974. He returned to Mallorca to join the conceptual avant-garde group Taller Llunàtic and had his first one-man show at the Palma Museum around 1976 at age 19. Rudi Fuchs discovered his work at a 1981 Madrid exhibition and invited him to Documenta 7.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond being born in Felanitx, Mallorca.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early art training, avant-garde collective, international exhibition exposure, neo-expressionism wave
evidence_summary: Barceló began formal art training in his teens, joined a conceptual avant-garde collective (Taller Llunàtic) by age 18, and had his first solo museum show by 19. His participation in Documenta 7 at 25 as the only Spanish artist marked his international breakthrough, riding the neo-expressionist wave of the early 1980s. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources; his early advantage appears self-created through immersion in the Mallorcan and Barcelona art scenes.
starting_point: Born in Felanitx, Mallorca; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Internationally renowned Spanish painter and sculptor; represented by major galleries including Acquavella Galleries New York and Galerie Bruno Bischofberger Zürich; decorated the UN Human Rights Council ceiling in Geneva (2008).

trajectory.event: Had his first one-man show at the Palma Museum in Mallorca after returning from brief studies at the Barcelona Fine Arts School.
Participated as the only Spanish artist in Documenta 7 in Kassel, Germany, gaining international recognition.
Received Spain's National Award for Plastic Arts.
Designed costumes and stage sets for Manuel de Falla's opera at the Opéra-Comique in Paris.
Watercolours illustrating Dante's Divine Comedy shown at the Louvre Museum in Paris, becoming the youngest artist exhibited there.
Inaugurated massive sculptural ceiling installation in the UN Human Rights Council room in Geneva, using 100 tons of paint.
Elected vice-president of CISAC and invested Doctor Honoris Causa by the University of Salamanca.

name: John Woo
milestone_by_age_26: Worked as script supervisor (1969, age 23) and assistant director at Shaw Studios (1971, age 25) but his directorial debut came in 1974 at age 28 with The Young Dragons. No material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Guangzhou, China, Woo's family fled to Hong Kong when he was five, living in poverty in the Shek Kip Mei slums. He was hired as a script supervisor at Cathay Studios in 1969 and became an assistant director at Shaw Studios in 1971, working under Chang Cheh.
family_context_summary: Born to an impoverished Protestant family in Guangzhou; father was a teacher incapacitated by tuberculosis, mother a construction laborer. Family fled to Hong Kong when Woo was five and was rendered homeless by the Shek Kip Mei fire of 1953.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; father was a teacher but unable to work due to tuberculosis.
evidence_summary: Woo grew up in severe poverty in Hong Kong slums after his family fled communist China. He entered the film industry at 23 as a script supervisor and became assistant director at Shaw Studios at 25, but his directorial debut did not come until age 28 in 1974. His breakthrough came much later with A Better Tomorrow in 1986 at age 40.

name: Masaaki Hatsumi
milestone_by_age_26: Met his teacher Toshitsugu Takamatsu at age 26 (1957), but this was the start of training, not a material achievement. He became grandmaster and founded the Bujinkan organization only after Takamatsu's death in 1972 at age 41. No material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Noda, Chiba, Hatsumi participated in sports and martial arts during school, achieved a black belt in judo at Meiji University, and taught judo to American soldiers at Yokota Air Base. He began kobudo training under Chosui Ueno and met Takamatsu at age 26, spending fifteen years as his student.
evidence_summary: Hatsumi trained in judo and other martial arts during university but only met his defining teacher Takamatsu at age 26. His grandmaster status and founding of the Bujinkan came at 41, well after age 26. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Peter Cosgrove
milestone_by_age_26: Awarded the Military Cross in 1971 at age 23-24 for gallantry during assault on enemy positions in Vietnam as a platoon commander with 9RAR.
early_history_summary: Born in Sydney, Cosgrove followed his father, a warrant officer, into the Australian Army by attending the Royal Military College, Duntroon in 1965. He was commissioned as a lieutenant in December 1968 and posted to Vietnam in August 1969 with the 9th Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment, where he commanded 5 Platoon, B Company and led multiple assaults on enemy bunker systems in October 1969.
family_context_summary: Born in Sydney; father was a warrant officer in the Australian Army, providing a military family background. Uncle Bill Cosgrove was a professional Australian rules footballer killed in WWII.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a warrant officer in the Australian Army, which influenced Cosgrove's decision to attend Duntroon and pursue a military career.
primary_early_advantage_tags: military family, Duntroon academy, combat command, gallantry award, platoon leadership
evidence_summary: Cosgrove grew up in a military family—his father was a warrant officer—and entered the Royal Military College, Duntroon at 18. Commissioned at 21, he was posted to Vietnam at 22 where he led infantry platoon assaults on enemy positions, earning the Military Cross at 23-24. His early advantage came from the elite military pipeline (Duntroon) and family military background, combined with direct combat domain exposure at a young age.
starting_point: Born in Sydney, Australia; father was a warrant officer in the Australian Army, providing a modest military family background.
current_position: Retired General and former Governor-General of Australia (2014-2019); served as Administrator of the Commonwealth briefly in 2023; resides in Australia.

trajectory.event: Commissioned as a lieutenant from the Royal Military College, Duntroon.
Posted to Vietnam with 9RAR; led platoon assaults on enemy bunker systems in October 1969.
Awarded the Military Cross for gallantry during combat operations in Vietnam.
Commanded the 1st Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment.
Led INTERFET peacekeeping mission in East Timor, achieving national prominence.
Promoted to General and appointed Chief of the Defence Force.
Sworn in as the 26th Governor-General of Australia.

name: Wang Shu
milestone_by_age_26: Completed a bachelor's degree in 1985 (age 22) and master's in 1988 (age 25), but his first architectural project was a youth centre in Haining in 1990 at age 27. No material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Ürümqi, Xinjiang, Wang began drawing and painting as a child without formal art training. He studied architecture at Southeast University in Nanjing, receiving his bachelor's in 1985 and master's in 1988. He then worked for the Zhejiang Academy of Fine Arts and completed his first architectural project in 1990.
family_context_summary: Born in Ürümqi to parents who recommended engineering; mother gave him access to a library during the Cultural Revolution. Family background otherwise not documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; parents recommended engineering as a compromise with his passion for art.
evidence_summary: Wang studied architecture at Southeast University (bachelor's 1985, master's 1988) but did not complete his first architectural project until 1990 at age 27. He had no commissions between 1990 and 1998 and earned a PhD in 2000. His Pritzker Prize came in 2012 at age 49. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Maryna Viazovska
milestone_by_age_26: Won first place at the International Mathematics Competition for University Students in 2005 (age 21) and co-authored her first research paper in 2005; completed a PhD in 2010 (age 25-26). These are student-level achievements and standard degrees. Her landmark sphere-packing solution came in 2016 at age 32, and the Fields Medal in 2022. No material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Kyiv, Viazovska attended a specialized science school and competed in domestic math Olympiads. She studied at Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv, competed at the International Mathematics Competition for University Students (first place 2002 and 2005), earned a master's from Kaiserslautern in 2007, and a PhD from the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine in 2010.
family_context_summary: Born in Kyiv; father was a chemist at the Antonov aircraft factory, mother was an engineer. She was the oldest of three sisters.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were a chemist and engineer, providing a technical family environment but not specifically mathematical.
evidence_summary: Viazovska showed early mathematical promise through Olympiad competitions and university-level math contests, with first-place finishes in 2002 and 2005. She earned her PhD in 2010 at age 25-26, but her defining achievement—solving the sphere-packing problem in dimensions 8 and 24—came in 2016 at age 32, earning the Fields Medal in 2022. No material milestone by age 26 was found beyond student competitions and a standard doctoral degree.

name: Lee Jae-yong
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Samsung in 1991 at age 23 as a junior employee; held entry-level positions with no notable achievement by age 26. Became COO of Samsung Electronics in 2009 at age 41 and Chairman in 2022. No material milestone by age 26 found.

He joined Samsung in 1991 in a junior role, with a position created exclusively for him as Chief Customer Officer.
family_context_summary: Born into the Samsung controlling family; father Lee Kun-hee was chairman of Samsung, mother Hong Ra-hee. Born in Washington D.C. and raised in South Korea with elite education.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was chairman of Samsung, one of the largest conglomerates in South Korea, providing extraordinary inherited business platform and capital access.
evidence_summary: Lee was born into the Samsung controlling family with extraordinary inherited wealth and corporate platform. He joined Samsung in 1991 at 23 in a junior role but had no material personal achievement by age 26. His rise to COO (2009), vice chairman (2012), and chairman (2022) came decades later. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Piero Manzoni
milestone_by_age_26: Made his public debut as an artist in August 1956 at age 23 at the Mostra d'Arte Contemporanea at Soncino's Sforza Castle, and by age 26 had developed the Achrome series and co-founded the Azimut Gallery in Milan (1959).
early_history_summary: Born in Soncino, Italy as Count Meroni Manzoni di Chiosca e Poggiolo, Manzoni was self-taught as an artist. He debuted in August 1956 at the Fourth Fair of Soncino at the town's Sforza Castle. After visiting Yves Klein's Epoca Blu exhibition in January 1957, he developed the Achrome series—white, colourless paintings using gesso, kaolin, and other materials. He co-founded the Azimut Gallery in Milan in 1959 with Enrico Castellani.
family_context_summary: Born as Count Meroni Manzoni di Chiosca e Poggiolo, an aristocratic title; eldest of five children of Egisto Manzoni and Valeria Meroni. The family had noble lineage in Soncino, province of Cremona.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources that parents had art-world connections, though the aristocratic background may have provided cultural and social access.
primary_early_advantage_tags: aristocratic background, self-taught, avant-garde collective, Yves Klein influence, Castellani collaboration, Milan art scene
evidence_summary: Manzoni was born into Italian aristocracy (Count Manzoni di Chiosca e Poggiolo) and was self-taught as an artist. He debuted publicly at 23 in 1956, and by 24 had developed the Achrome series after encountering Yves Klein's monochromes. By 26, he co-founded the Azimut Gallery with Enrico Castellani in Milan, positioning himself at the centre of the European avant-garde. His aristocratic background may have provided social access, but his artistic innovation was largely self-driven through intense collaboration with peers like Castellani and engagement with the Milan art scene.
starting_point: Born as Count Piero Meroni Manzoni di Chiosca e Poggiolo in Soncino, Italy; eldest of five children in an aristocratic family.
current_position: Died February 6, 1963 in Milan at age 29 from myocardial infarction; final role: avant-garde artist whose work prefigured Conceptual Art and influenced Arte Povera.

trajectory.event: Made his public debut as an artist at the Mostra d'Arte Contemporanea at Sforza Castle in Soncino in August 1956.
Developed the Achrome series after visiting Yves Klein's Epoca Blu exhibition, shifting to white, colourless paintings.
Co-founded the Azimut Gallery in Milan with Enrico Castellani and launched the journal Azimuth.
Created Artist's Shit (Merda d'Artista), 90 sealed cans priced by weight at the value of gold, his most famous work.
Died of a heart attack in his Milan studio on February 6, 1963; friend Ben Vautier signed his death certificate declaring it a work of art.

name: Tomas Lindahl
milestone_by_age_26: Was a doctoral student at Karolinska Institutet; PhD came in 1967 at age 29 and MD in 1970 at age 32. Nobel Prize in Chemistry came in 2015 at age 77. No material milestone by age 26 found.

He did postdoctoral research at Princeton and Rockefeller Universities before becoming a professor at the University of Gothenburg in 1978.
family_context_summary: Born to Folke Robert Lindahl and Ethel Hulda Hultberg in Stockholm, Sweden. Family background otherwise not documented.
evidence_summary: Lindahl was a doctoral student at Karolinska Institutet during his early twenties but did not complete his PhD until age 29 in 1967. His pioneering DNA repair research and Nobel Prize came much later in life. No material milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Narendra Dabholkar
milestone_by_age_26: Was a national-level Kabaddi player who represented India against Bangladesh and won the Maharashtra government's Shiv Chhatrapati Award for Kabaddi, but no specific dated year for these achievements could be found to confirm they occurred by age 26. Founded MANS in 1989 at age 44. No specifically dated material milestone by age 26 found.
early_history_summary: Born in Satara, British India as the youngest of ten children in a Brahmin family, Dabholkar attended New English School Satara and Willingdon College, Sangli. He was captain of the Shivaji University Kabaddi team, represented India against Bangladesh, and won the Shiv Chhatrapati Sports Award and Youth Award for Kabaddi. He obtained an MBBS from Government Medical College, Miraj.
family_context_summary: Born as the youngest of ten children in a Brahmin household in Satara; elder siblings included educationalist and socialist Devdatta Dabholkar and Shripad Dabholkar. Family was academically and socially engaged.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources that family had specific sports connections, though the family was well-educated and socially active.
evidence_summary: Dabholkar was a national-level Kabaddi player who captained the Shivaji University team and represented India against Bangladesh, winning the Shiv Chhatrapati Award. The Shiv Chhatrapati Award was instituted in 1969-70 when Dabholkar was 24-25, but his name does not appear in available Kabaddi awardee lists, and the exact year of his award is undocumented. His main life work—founding MANS—came at age 44 in 1989.

name: Fedor Emelianenko
milestone_by_age_26: Won the PRIDE Heavyweight Championship on March 16, 2003 at age 26 by unanimous decision over Antônio Rodrigo Nogueira, becoming one of the most dominant champions in MMA history. Also won the RINGS Heavyweight Class Championship in February 2001 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Born in Rubizhne, Ukrainian SSR, Emelianenko moved to Stary Oskol, Russia at age two. He began sambo and judo at age 11 under Vladimir Voronov, earned Master of Sport certification in 1997 at age 21, and served in the Russian Army from 1995-1997. He joined the Russian national judo/sambo team and won a European sambo championship gold in 1999 before transitioning to professional MMA in 2000 due to financial need.
family_context_summary: Born to a teacher mother and welder father in Rubizhne, Ukrainian SSR; family moved to Stary Oskol, Russia when he was two. Parents divorced during his military service. Working-class family with no notable athletic lineage documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; parents were a teacher and welder with no documented martial arts background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early sambo/judo training, sustained coaching, combat sambo pipeline, financial hardship catalyst, Russian national team
evidence_summary: Emelianenko began sambo and judo at age 11 under coach Vladimir Voronov, who provided sustained individualized training for over a decade. He earned Master of Sport certification at 21, won European sambo gold at 23, and transitioned to MMA at 24 due to financial hardship. By 26, he won the PRIDE Heavyweight Championship, the most prestigious title in MMA at the time. His early advantage came from deep technical reps in sambo/judo from a young age, a dedicated long-term coach, and the Russian combat sambo pipeline, compounded by financial urgency that drove his professional fighting career.
starting_point: Born to a teacher mother and welder father in Rubizhne, Ukrainian SSR; working-class family that moved to Stary Oskol, Russia when he was two.
current_position: Retired from professional MMA in February 2023 with a record of 40 wins, 7 losses, 1 no contest; widely considered one of the greatest MMA heavyweights of all time; serves as president of Russian MMA Union and deputy of Belgorod Regional Duma.

trajectory.event: Received Master of Sport certification in judo and sambo and joined the Russian national team.
Won European Combat Sambo Championship gold in Istanbul and bronze in Russian judo championships.
Won the RINGS Heavyweight Class Championship after Bobby Hoffman forfeited in the King of Kings tournament final.
Won the PRIDE Heavyweight Championship by unanimous decision over Antônio Rodrigo Nogueira at PRIDE 25 on March 16, 2003.
Won the PRIDE 2004 Heavyweight World Grand Prix tournament.
Won combat sambo world championship gold in Prague.
Originally retired from MMA with a record of 34-4; elected as deputy of the Belgorod Regional Duma.
Retired for the second and final time on February 4, 2023, with a career record of 40-7-1.
